facts.fact: At dawn, with the east line dark, Kunal says Ranu's runners can reach Sarn fold by dusk through the low lanes (no rope needed there), faster than a bound pair; he cannot go himself and hates sending others. Before dark he sends a red-thread walnut to Sarn fold by Nimmi's eldest runner.
The thirty-second grave at Ranu is a man who had nursed all the sick; Rohan held the rope while it was dug.
The red-thread walnut as a route-keepers' true-word token has been kept ten generations; a message without one is a lie or not from Kunal's people.

Ila marks nine crosses on her sheet where the salt road breaks the law (a ford on the closed side of the border stones, a gap in a boundary wall, a goat-bridge over a toll gully, six more), plus a stone-ringed halting hollow with a soot-black hearth in the lee of the second spur, where Nimmi's runners sleep.
Kunal chose the salt road as a test of whether Ila would draw a true road that could hang men; Ila realises it and he admits it.
A grave at Ranu carries a spinning top (replaces the bell on a grave in the earlier draft, to avoid echoing Sunni's buried bell).
